newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bids $66-$67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bids $66-$67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $66.00 to $67.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said. There were no reported trades.
The bulk of last week's sales were at $68.00. Prices this week could trade steady, unless beef prices continue weak, the sources said.

Light demand last week pushed beef prices lower, with the choice heavyweight price sliding $1.21 per cwt for the week at $105.97, USDA statistics showed. Beef prices at midday were slightly lower in light activity.
Beef prices were quoted down $0.04 to $0.31, with 34 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said. Choice heavyweight beef was quoted down $0.04 at $105.93.
Gains in fed cattle prices this week could be muted by increased supplies of finished cattle following a carryover from last week's, sources said.
Showlists in the Panhandle were estimated near 94,000 head, up 10,000 from last week. The Kansas showlist was estimated near 80,000 head, up 5,000, market sources said.
